key_findings.statement: The policy covers eye surgery as a day care procedure if it meets the 24-hour waiver criteria due to technological advancement or specialized infrastructure requirements.
Cataract surgery is subject to a 1-year waiting period in the first year of cover, which can be waived if the insured has completed years of continuous coverage under a previous policy.
The insured has 29 months of continuous coverage, but the policy requires completed years for the waiting period waiver and receipt of claim history from the previous insurer.
Pre and post hospitalization expenses are reimbursable if connected to the admitted condition, but the connection and timing relative to the admission date are not explicitly verified.
The policy requires hospital registration or compliance with all minimum criteria; the supplied facts establish neither route.

citations.section: WHAT WE COVER / NB4: The hospitalisation treatment of Insured Person as inpatient in the Hospital/Nursing Home for a
citations.quote:
NB4: The hospitalisation treatment of Insured Person as inpatient in the Hospital/Nursing Home for a
minimum period of 24 hours for specific treatment like Dialysis, Chemotherapy, Radiotherapy, Eye
Surgery, Lithotripsy, Tonsillectomy or D&C(medical expenses for 140 Day Care Procedures enlisted
in the Annexure to this Policy Wordings) shall also be covered under the Policy.
The minimum stay of 24 hours can be waived in other cases also provided that the following
conditions are fulfilled:
a) The treatment is such that it necessitates Hospitalisation and procedure involved requires
specialised infrastructure facilities available in the Hospital.
Or
b) Due to technological advances, the period of Hospitalisation for the treatment has been reduced to
less than 24 hours.

citations.claim: The policy covers eye surgery as a day care procedure if it meets the 24-hour waiver criteria due to technological advancement or specialized infrastructure requirements.
citations.quote:
Day Care Treatment
Day care treatment refers to medical treatment, and/or surgical procedure which is:
i. undertaken under General or Local Anesthesia in a hospital/day care centre in less than 24 hrs
because of technological advancement, and
ii. which would have otherwise required a hospitalization of more than 24 hours.
Treatment normally taken on an out-patient basis is not included in the scope of this definition.

3. Hospitalization expense incurred in the first year of operation of the insurance cover on treatment of the

i) Cataract

xiv) Gastric and duodenal ulcers
However, a waiting period of 1 year will not apply if You were insured continuously and without interruption

reimbursement of medical costs for inpatient treatment in a Hospital.

 We will only apply the reduction of the waiting period if We have received the database and claim
history from the previous Indian insurance Company (if applicable);
 We are under no obligation to insure all Insured Persons or to insure all Insured Persons on the
proposed terms, or on the same terms as the previous health insurance Policy even if You have
submitted to Us all documentation
 We shall consider only completed years of coverage for waiver of waiting periods.

semantic_checks.explanation: The policy explicitly lists eye surgery as a procedure that can be covered as a day care procedure if it meets the 24-hour waiver criteria due to technological advancement or specialized infrastructure.
The policy lists cataract as a condition subject to a 1-year waiting period and provides for a waiver if the insured was continuously insured for at least 1 year under a previous policy.

The policy requires completed years of coverage and receipt of claim history from the previous insurer to waive the waiting period, and the case facts confirm the insured has 29 months of coverage but lacks the required prior insurer history.

The policy allows for pre and post hospitalization expenses within specified timeframes (30 and 60 days respectively), but the case facts do not provide the specific dates required to verify the connection and timing.
The policy defines a hospital based on registration or specific minimum criteria; the case facts only state the facility is a network provider, which does not satisfy the definition requirements.
The policy limits doctor fees to 25% of the Sum Insured (125,000 INR), and the claim of 15,000 INR is within this limit.
The policy limits medicines and diagnostics to 40% of the Sum Insured (200,000 INR), and the claim of 45,000 INR is within this limit.
